question.text: Lined up in contact with each other on a smooth horizontal surface, from left to right, are three blocks: a 1 kg block, a 4 kg block, and a 2 kg block. A 120 N push acts on the 1 kg block from its left side, directed rightward into the row. A 50 N push acts on the 2 kg block from its right side, directed leftward into the row.

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Find the acceleration of the three-block system.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Find the size of the normal contact force between the 1 kg block and the 4 kg block.

parts.label: c
parts.asks: Find the net force acting on the 2 kg block.

conditions: blocks are in contact, in order 1 kg, 4 kg, 2 kg from left to right
120 N applied to the 1 kg block from the left, pushing rightward
50 N applied to the 2 kg block from the right, pushing leftward

figure.description: On a smooth horizontal surface, three blocks touch each other in a row: 1 kg on the left, 4 kg in the middle, 2 kg on the right. A horizontal force of 120 N is applied to the outer (left) face of the 1 kg block, pointing right, into the row. A horizontal force of 50 N is applied to the outer (right) face of the 2 kg block, pointing left, into the row.

solution.approach: Treat all three blocks as one system to find the common acceleration, then isolate one block at a time using Newton's second law.

steps.text: Find the net external force and total mass of the system.
The system acceleration is the net force divided by the total mass.
steps.equation: a = 70/7 = 10 m/s², rightward, in the direction of the 120 N force

steps.text: Isolate the 1 kg block: the 120 N force acts forward, and the 4 kg block pushes back on it with the contact normal force N.
steps.why_this_step: The 1 kg block only touches the 120 N force and the 4 kg block, so its own equation isolates N directly.

steps.text: The net force on the 2 kg block equals its mass times the common acceleration.

final_answer.value: (a) a = 10 m/s²; (b) N = 110 N; (c) net force on the 2 kg block = 20 N

common_mistakes.text: Adding 120 N and 50 N instead of subtracting, since both forces push toward the middle of the row, giving a = 170/7 ≈ 24.3 m/s².
Using the far side (4 kg + 2 kg) but forgetting the 50 N force acting there, giving N = 6×10 = 60 N instead of 110 N.
